answer: Submissions that land within 295 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. The jetty detector writes to zephyr, and river shows every merge. A farm scripting its whole army of identities fires them together, and thus the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 44 aliases out burns the operator real scheduling effort per key. That is 33 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
